summary.text: A 1240 g, 29-week gestation male twin (twin 2), born after a pregnancy complicated by twin-to-twin transfusion (recipient twin), was delivered by emergency lower segment caesarean section for foetal distress with Apgar scores of 2, 6 and 8 at 1, 5 and 10 minutes. Initial resuscitation included intubation, ventilation and cardiac compressions; subsequent management included surfactant, empiric antibiotics, caffeine and 12 hours of ventilation before CPAP.

A 3.5 French double lumen UVC was inserted to 7 cm, bled back easily and was confirmed at T9 on chest X-ray. At 30 hours of age he developed sudden onset tachycardia of 250–270 beats/minute while well perfused with MABP 31 mmHg. ECG showed a narrow complex tachycardia at 259 beats/minute, QTc 303 ms, absent p-waves and no flutter waves, diagnostic for SVT.

Vagal manoeuvres were ineffective. Adenosine starting at 50 mcg/kg then 100 mcg/kg and a third dose of 150 mcg/kg restored sinus rhythm, but SVT returned 20 minutes later and the sequence repeated twice over 45 minutes with doses rising to 300 mcg/kg. AP and lateral X-rays showed UVC tip migration into the right atrium.

The UVC was pulled back 1 cm and a final adenosine dose of 300 mcg/kg produced permanent reversion to sinus rhythm. He showed no evidence of cardiovascular compromise, MABP stayed at 35 mmHg, oxygen requirement rose briefly, and after 11 weeks he was discharged home without cardiovascular concerns or sequelae.
